newsitem.title: USA: H&R Block reports higher profits for quarter.
newsitem.headline: H&R Block reports higher profits for quarter.

text.p: Tax preparation firm H&R Block Inc. Wednesday reported higher profits for the fourth quarter but a sharp drop in earnings for the fiscal year due to losses at its majority-owned CompuServe online service.

For its fiscal fourth quarter ended April 30, Block said its earnings rose to $199.4 million, or $1.90 a share, from $185.7 million, or $1.75 a share, in the year-ago quarter. Revenues rose to $1.09 billion from $922 million.
Kansas City, Mo.-based Block said its full-year earnings, however, were hurt by a $186.5 million pretax loss reported by CompuServe Corp., of which Block owns 80.1 percent.

For the full year, Block said its profits fell to $47.8 million, or 45 cents a share, from $177.2 million, or $1.67 a share, in the prior fiscal year. Revenues rose to $1.93 billion from $1.66 billion.
Excluding CompuServe's results, Block said revenues rose nearly 26 percent from $871.5 million last year to $1.1 billion for fiscal 1997.

"Clearly without CompuServe's results, H&R Block exceeded its goals to grow revenues and earnings by 15 percent," Chief Executive Officer Frank Salizzoni said in a statement. "H&R Block Tax Services, H&R Block International and Block Financial all contributed to these strong results."
For the full year, pretax earnings at H&R Block Tax Services Inc. rose nearly 12 percent to $204.3 million. Block International's pretax earnings rose nearly 21 percent to $14.2 million.
In the United States, H&R Block prepared 14.2 million tax returns, a 7.1 percent increase over the previous year.

H&R Block also named Ozzie Wenich, 54, senior vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer, replacing George Robson, who resigned June 1. Wenich, currently president of H&R Block International, will retain that title.
H&R Block's stock was down $1.625 at $33.125 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
